Proposes an approach (XRepoSkill, trajectory-based learning of transferable skill rules for SE agents); secondary: compares (vs no-skill agent and three skill-learning methods on two benchmarks with three LLMs)
XRepoSkill (authors' own, no version; code released). Baselines: raw mini-SWE-agent 2.0 (no skills), SkillOpt, STAIR, Trace2Skill (versions Not stated)

Skill = one Markdown file of transferable rules (title, tag with gain and z score, body), each rule with an executable predicate over abstract actions; 36 transferable rules learned; up to 3 rules selected per issue and placed above the issue description in the first user message

Stage 1 divergence-guided rule discovery (pair successful/failed trajectories, action abstraction, divergence point, three prompts generate candidate rules + predicates) -> Stage 2 within-repository merging and verification (Mantel-Haenszel resolution gain, z score), cross-repository clustering (phi correlation), LLM consolidation into transferable rules (>=2 repos) -> Stage 3 issue-adaptive selection (two backbone-LLM calls, <=3 rules) -> skill-guided resolution by unchanged agent

Tasks: 200 sampled SWE-bench Pro tasks (no .git history, no network) + 113 DeepSWE tasks (official environment); no evaluation repository in the learning pool. Configurations: 5 methods x 3 backbone LLMs (reasoning effort high). Baseline: mini-SWE-agent without skills. Held constant: same agent, system prompt, tool interface, step and cost limits; skills of all methods learned from the same pool with the same LLM (DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813); methods differ only in text before the issue. Acceptance: benchmark tests (hidden tests in DeepSWE). Repetitions: single run per issue, except 4 runs in RQ3 (DeepSWE, DeepSeek). Human intervention: none

XRepoSkill best in all 6 benchmark-LLM cells. SWE-bench Pro average 53.8% vs mini-SWE-agent 47.8 (+6.0) and STAIR 51.7 (+2.1); DeepSWE average 44.2% vs 33.9 (+10.3) and Trace2Skill 39.2 (+5.0). Repeated runs: +13.0 over mini-SWE-agent and +9.3 over Trace2Skill, 95% CIs not overlapping. Cost similar: $0.11 vs $0.09-0.12 per issue (SWE-Pro), $0.25 vs $0.18-0.22 (DeepSWE). Cross-language gains larger on non-Python languages (e.g., TypeScript DeepSWE +21.0 vs STAIR); Python on par

Distinguished methods consistently in direction; significance only shown for DeepSWE with DeepSeek (4 runs, CIs). Limitations noted: SWE-bench Pro sampled (200 of 731) for budget; container without git history/network not comparable to official images; small language subsets (5-6 issues) to be read with caution; gain per rule confounded by joint selection

No limitations or threats section. Stated caveats: budget-limited sampling and single runs; small per-language subsets; selected-rule gains belong to the selected set, not one rule; a third of the skill almost unused
